subject: Literacy
title: Sound games with s, a, t, p
objectives: Children will play games with the sounds /s/ /a/ /t/ /p/.
Children will sort objects by their first sound with support.
content: Playing games with the four sounds: a sound hunt, sorting by first sound and sound bingo.
teachingActivities: Keep every game playful; say the sound first before showing the picture; always use pure sounds; accept a point or a sound; keep the number of choices small for children who find it hard.
learnerActivities: Play games with /s/ /a/ /t/ /p/ and sort objects by their first sound with support.
resources: Objects and pictures for s, a, t and p
Four baskets labelled with a picture
assessment: Observe whether each child says at least two of the four sounds and sorts by first sound with support.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures by first sound with support.
Says at least two of the four sounds.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: taking turns in games

lessons.title: Four sounds hunt
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find objects that start with the four sounds in a hunt.
successCriteria: Finds an object and says its first sound
Names at least two of the sounds
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/, /a/, /t/ and /p/ and find objects that start with each.
resources: Eight objects: sun, sock, ant, apple, tap, tin, pot, pan
lessons.starter: Say "sss, a, t, p. Four sounds. Let us hunt for things that start with them." Show the baskets.
teacherActivities: Show each basket and say its sound: sss for the snake, a for the ant, t for the tap, p for the pot.
Hide the eight objects in easy places in the room.
Say "Find something" and let each child bring one object to the mat.
Say the word, then the first sound, then put it in the matching basket.
learnerActivities: Child says the first sound and places it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each basket and say its sound: sss for the snake, a for the ant, t for the tap, p for the pot. Children: Children say each sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Hide the eight objects in easy places in the room. Children: Children watch.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Find something" and let each child bring one object to the mat. Children: Child finds an object.
Step 4. Teacher: Say the word, then the first sound, then put it in the matching basket. Children: Child says the first sound and places it.

practical.title: Sound hunt
steps: Hide eight objects in easy places.
Say the first sound and put it in the right basket.
practical.safety: Hide objects in clear, low places away from hazards. Supervise the search and keep children together.

differentiation.support: Use two baskets only and say the sound with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two objects for the same basket.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sound does sun start with?
Which basket does apple go in?

expectedOutcomes: Finds and sorts objects by first sound with support
Says at least two of the sounds
lessons.conclusion: Count the objects in each basket and say the sounds.
lessons.homeConnection: Hunt for things at home that start with sss, a, t or p.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find objects that start with the four sounds in a hunt" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sorting by sound
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will sort pictures by their first sound.
successCriteria: Puts a picture in the right sound basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/, /a/, /t/ and /p/ and find objects that start with each.
resources: Picture cards for each of the four sounds
lessons.starter: Say "I have pictures. Which sound do they start with? Let us sort them."
teacherActivities: Pick a card, say the word and its first sound, and put it in the right basket.
Pick another card and ask "Which basket?"
Let each child pick a card and sort it.
Check each basket together by saying the words.
learnerActivities: Child sorts the card and says the sound.
Children say the words and the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick a card, say the word and its first sound, and put it in the right basket. Children: Children say the first sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick another card and ask "Which basket?" Children: Child points to the basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick a card and sort it. Children: Child sorts the card and says the sound.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each basket together by saying the words. Children: Children say the words and the sound.

practical.title: Sound sort
steps: Put four baskets on the mat.
Each child picks a card and says its first sound.
Put it in the right basket.
practical.safety: Use large soft cards. Keep children seated with room to reach and supervise turns.

differentiation.support: Offer two baskets and say the sound very clearly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort five cards without help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which basket does tin go in?
What sound does pan start with?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures by first sound with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the cards away and say each sound.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort toys by their first sound at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort pictures by their first sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sound bingo
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will play a simple bingo game with the four sounds.
successCriteria: Covers the matching picture on the card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/, /a/, /t/ and /p/ and find objects that start with each.
resources: Bingo cards with four pictures each
lessons.starter: Show a bingo card and say "I will say a sound. You cover the picture."
teacherActivities: Say "sss" and ask the children to cover the snake picture with a counter.
Say "a" and ask them to cover the ant picture.
Let a child say a sound and the others cover.
learnerActivities: Children cover each picture as they hear the sound.
Child calls a sound and friends cover.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "sss" and ask the children to cover the snake picture with a counter. Children: Children cover the picture.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "a" and ask them to cover the ant picture. Children: Children cover the picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Continue with t and p. Children: Children cover each picture as they hear the sound.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child say a sound and the others cover. Children: Child calls a sound and friends cover.

practical.title: Sound bingo
steps: Give each child a card and counters.
Say a sound and children cover the picture.
Play until the card is covered.
practical.safety: Use large counters that cannot be swallowed or use stickers. Supervise counters closely.

differentiation.support: Use a card with two pictures and help cover the picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to call the sounds for a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which picture do you cover for t?

expectedOutcomes: Matches sounds to pictures in a game
Says some of the four sounds
lessons.conclusion: Count the covered pictures together and clap.
lessons.homeConnection: Play bingo at home with pictures and the four sounds.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a simple bingo game with the four sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sound song and actions
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will sing a song with all four sounds and their actions.
successCriteria: Does the right action for each sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/, /a/, /t/ and /p/ and find objects that start with each.
resources: Picture cards: snake, ant, tap, pot
lessons.starter: Show the four cards and say "Sss for snake. A for ant. T for tap. P for pot."
teacherActivities: Sing "Sss for snake, a for ant, t for tap, p for pot" and show each card.
Sing again and do each action: wiggle, crawl, tap, pop.
Say a sound and let children do the action.
Let a child choose a card and lead.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing "Sss for snake, a for ant, t for tap, p for pot" and show each card. Children: Children listen and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and do each action: wiggle, crawl, tap, pop. Children: Children do each action.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a sound and let children do the action. Children: Child does the matching action.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child choose a card and lead. Children: Child leads and friends follow.

practical.title: Four sounds game
steps: Stand in a circle with space.
Say a sound and everyone does the action.
practical.safety: Clear the floor and keep movements small. Stop when children are tired.

differentiation.support: Do the actions together and say the sound very clearly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the game by choosing the next sound.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do for sss?
What do we do for p?

lessons.conclusion: Sing quietly and wave goodbye to the four sounds.
lessons.homeConnection: Do the four sound actions at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a song with all four sounds and their actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 four sounds check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child hears, says and sorts the four sounds.
successCriteria: Says at least two of the four sounds
Sorts by first sound with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say /s/, /a/, /t/ and /p/ and find objects that start with each.
lessons.starter: Say "sss, a, t, p" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sort, bingo and hunt.
At each station ask "What sound?" and watch what the child can do.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child says the sound or points.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sort, bingo and hunt. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What sound?" and watch what the child can do. Children: Child says the sound or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Four sound stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large soft cards and counters.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two sounds.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend a sound.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says /s/ /a/ /t/ /p/; sorts by first sound with support; plays the sound games.

questions.question: What sound does sun start with?
What sound does pot start with?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
Says at least two of the sounds
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the four sounds.
lessons.homeConnection: Play sound games at home with sss, a, t and p.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child hears, says and sorts the four sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
